regular_terms.source_quote: 9.1 Regular Terms. Decisions on students' academic standing and progress are made only at the end of the Fall and the Spring Terms, which are referred to as Regular Terms.
regular_terms.note: Winter and Summer are academic terms but not Regular Terms, so the AR 5.4 load limits do not apply to them.

academic_terms.source_quote: There are four academic terms in each academic year: Fall (normally early September to late December); Winter; Spring (normally early February to late May); and Summer (normally late June to mid-August).

min_credits_regular_term.source_quote: 5.4 Maximum and Minimum Study Load. In each Regular Term, students within their normative duration of study and in good academic standing must register for courses totalling a mimimum of 12 credits and a maximum of 18 credits.
min_credits_regular_term.note: The spelling "mimimum" is the official page's. Applies to students within their normative duration and in good academic standing.

max_credits_regular_term.source_quote: 5.4 Maximum and Minimum Study Load. In each Regular Term, students within their normative duration of study and in good academic standing must register for courses totalling a mimimum of 12 credits and a maximum of 18 credits.

overload_approval.source_quote: Students seeking an exemption from AR 5.4 require the approval of the relevant Dean or the Dean's designee.
overload_approval.note: An exemption is possible but no ceiling is published, so no higher limit may be assumed. A plan above 18 credits is an error unless the student says the exemption is already approved.

min_credits_summer_term.note: Not found. AR 5.4 is written for Regular Terms, and Summer is not one. Validators must warn "verify" rather than apply 12-18.

min_credits_winter_term.note: Not found; Winter is not a Regular Term.

max_credits_winter_term.note: Not found; Winter is not a Regular Term.

graduation_total_credits.source_quote: 4.1 Requirements for Bachelor's Degrees. To gain an award of a bachelor's degree, students are required to: i. Earn at least 120 credits in approved courses or through credit transfer subject to AR 6.3.

graduation_other_requirements.source_quote: 4.1 ... ii. Fulfill the requirements of the University Common Core Program iii. Fulfill the University English Language Requirement iv. Fulfill the University Legal Education Requirement [For students admitted in 2022-23 intake or after only] v. Fulfill School/ AIS requirements, if any, for programs under the School/ AIS vi. Fulfill requirements for at least one Major, or School requirements for a general degree under the School
graduation_other_requirements.note: The English and Legal Education requirements are not modelled as rules; no course list for them was collected in Phase 1.

min_hkust_credits.source_quote: 6.3 Minimum HKUST Credits. To graduate with bachelor degree(s) from the University, students must complete a minimum of two years of full-time study at HKUST and obtain a minimum of 60 HKUST course credits.
min_hkust_credits.note: This caps transferred credits at 60 for a 120-credit degree. The AR adds that a Major, Minor or the Common Core Program may specify its own minimum.

min_years_at_hkust.source_quote: ... students must complete a minimum of two years of full-time study at HKUST and obtain a minimum of 60 HKUST course credits.

transfer_credit_types.source_quote: Transfer of credit can be of three types: (i) course-credit transfer, where a transferred course is equivalent to a specific course in the HKUST course catalog; (ii) credit-only transfer, where only credits are transferred; (iii) cross-campus transfer, where both credits and grades attained by students in courses offered by HKUST(GZ) via "cross-campus study" are automatically transferred.
transfer_credit_types.note: "credit-only transfer" is the official name for the intake form's "unspecified credits" rows. Only course-credit transfer maps to a named HKUST course.

transfer_credits_count_toward_gpa.source_quote: Transfer credits granted for (i) and (ii) will not be included in the calculation of grade averages, unless prior arrangements have been made.

additional_major_single_counted_credits.source_quote: To graduate with an Additional Major, students must fulfill the requirements specified for that Major, within which they must complete at least 20 single-counted credits. These 20 credits cannot be used to fulfill any other requirements for graduation except for the 120-credit degree requirement.
additional_major_single_counted_credits.note: Applies to an additional major, not to a minor.

common_core_reuse_allowed.source_quote: Under the new 30-credit Common Core Program which is applicable to students admitted to the University in 2022-23 and thereafter, courses that have been counted towards School and/or Major Requirements are not allowed to be reused for fulfilment of the University Common Core Requirements.
common_core_reuse_allowed.note: Printed in the preamble of every program requirement PDF. This is the one double-counting rule with a clear source: Major/School credits may never also be Common Core credits.

major_minor_double_count_cap.note: No University-wide cap was found. Each minor states its own floor instead: the minor PDFs collected say "at least 9 credits ... should be single-counted within the minor and are not used to fulfill any other requirements for graduation except the 120-credit degree requirement". planner/allocate.py must read that per program from Program.max_double_count_credits and warn "verify" where it is null.

minor_total_credits.note: Not set by the AR. Every minor PDF collected states its own minimum, 18 credits in each case; that figure is in each data/programs/MINOR-*.json rather than here.

exchange_credit_rules.note: Not found. AR 6 covers credit transfer in general and makes no statement specific to outgoing exchange. planner/validate.py must therefore treat every exchange mapping as pending approval and warn "verify", never as satisfied (hard rule 6).

fyp_duration_terms.note: Not found. The AR says nothing about Final Year Project duration, and no program PDF collected states that an FYP must span two terms. check_fyp must warn "verify" rather than assume.

max_online_credits.source_quote: Students may use no more than 9 credits earned from courses delivered in online mode, including HKUST self-paced online [SPO] courses and other online credits approved through the University's credit transfer procedures, to satisfy the graduation requirements of a degree program.
max_online_credits.note: Printed in the preamble of every program requirement PDF. Not checked by any validator: data/catalog.json records no delivery mode, because the course pages state it only for some courses.
